This Mfa Is Filed U/S. 173 (1) Of Motor Vehicles Act,
 1988, Against The Judgment And Award Dated 18.04.2016
 Passed In Mvc No. 950/2015 On The File Of The Member Iii
 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At Ballari, Partly
 Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And Seeking
 Enhancement Of Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
 Vijaykumar A.Patil, J. Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimants are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation, not being satisfied with the compensation awarded under judgment and award dated 18.04.2016 passed in MVC No.950/2015 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari (for short, 'Tribunal').
2.

The claimants, who are the children and husband of the deceased Rathna, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of deceased Rathna that took place on 02.11.2014 involving bus bearing registration No.KA-19/D-2715,
and lorry tanker bearing registration No.KA-14/A-7799.
It is stated that the deceased was aged about 51 years as on the date of the accident and she was the only earning member earning Rs.15,000/- per month from tailoring.

2 3.
The respondents Nos.1 to 3 remained absent and hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.4-insurance Company filed their statement of objections denying the claim averments made in the claim petition.
Respondent No.4-Insurane company inter-alia denied the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle.

It was contended that there were no materials available to show that,
the accident occurred only on the sole reason that driver was driving in rash and negligent manner.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The Tribunal has framed issues and recorded evidence.
1st claimant-son and 3rd claimant-husband of the deceased examined themselves as PW-1 and PW-2 respectively and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P12.
Respondents did not examine any witness, and produced only insurance policy which is marked as Ex.R1.

The Tribunal based on the material evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.5,15,088/- with interest at 6% per annum on the following heads:
1. Loss of Dependency Rs.4,40,088/-
2. Transportation of dead body And Funeral expenses, Rs.25,000/-
3. Loss of consortium to the 1st Claimant Rs.25,000/-
4. Loss of Estate Rs.25.000/-
Total Rs.5,15,088/-
5.

While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.5000/- per month, deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and applied multiplier of 11.
The claimants not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation.

6. Sri. M.B Hiremath, learned counsel for the appellants-claimants would submit that the notional income of the deceased was assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.5,000/-
per month is on the lower side, since the deceased was a tailor by profession and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

It is further submitted that as per the chart prepared by High Court Legal Services Authority the notional income of the deceased should have assessed at Rs.7500/- p.m. and the Tribunal has committed error in considering notional income as Rs.5,000/- which is on the lower side.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in not awarding any compensation towards future prospects.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal on other heads are also on lower side and sought for enhancement of compensation.

7. Per contra, Sri. S.S Joshi, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company supports the impunged judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the Tribunal has Sri.Karthik vs Sri.S B Jagadeesha on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16889525/
3 considered the evidence on record and assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/-
and applied 11 as multiplier and deducted 1/3 rd towards personal expenses.
Hence, it does not call for any interference in the present appeal.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the points that would arise for consideration in this appeal are,
1)Whether the Tribunal has justified in assessing the notional income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/-
p.m.?
2) Whether the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case?

9. The answer to the above points are negative & affirmative for the following reasons:
It is not in dispute that with regard to the accident in question and resultant death of Rathna, in the said accident.
The contention of the appellant/claimants that the Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5000/- per month.
In our considered view the in the absence of any evidence on record with regard to the income of the deceased, the Tribunal is required to assess the income of the deceased notionally.

Generally this Court and in Lok Adalaths while settling/adjudicating the claims arising out of the motor vehicle accident, rely on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authorities while assessing the income, the notional income has been assessed by Karnataka State Legal Services Authorities keeping in mind various factors.

The accident is of the year 2014 we base our reliance on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authorities and assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- p.m. in the absence of any evidence on record.
10. The Tribunal has committed error in not awarding any compensation towards the future prospects of the deceased.
Keeping in mind the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others.1

For the aforementioned reasons, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 18.04.2016 passed in MVC No.950/2015 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari is - 10 - modified and the appellant/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.3,60,912/- at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
iii) The respondent-insurance company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
iv) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.

v) Draw modified award accordingly.
vi) Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
vii) No order as to costs.
